newsitem.title: UK: London gold lower after OTC options, eyeing FOMC.
newsitem.headline: London gold lower after OTC options, eyeing FOMC.

text.p: Precious metals prices slid lower on Tuesday afternoon after speculative and options-related selling threatened to sweep the support out from under them.
Gold and silver prices took a hit following uneventful over-the-counter options expiry.
Platinum and palladium, meanwhile, starting tumbling earlier on news that strikes at a big Russian producer were postponed, dealers said.
Following the 1430 GMT expiry, gold crumbled below the psychological $350 an ounce level and fixed at $349.60 an ounce, $1.30 lower than in the morning.
Dealers reported fund selling in all the metals, with liquidation of options-related cover contributing to the drop.
"This scenario happens with amazing regularity after nearly every expiry. The palladium news out of Russia didn't help either," a dealer said.
Support for gold was expected to emerge at $348.50 and then the recent low of $345.30.
But the market still had to contend with an expected rise in U.S. interest rates by a meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.
The results of the FOMC were expected at 1915 GMT.

A forecast 25 basis points rate rise was priced into the market. In other markets, the dollar was still barely firmer against the yen, while Wall Street stocks extended a rally from Monday. Neither factor was supportive of gold, dealers said.
The white metals also headed south after fund selling piled into the market in the afternoon.
Silver, which had held around the $5.15 key strike price for most of the day, dove to a low bid of $5.07 after the expiry before bouncing slightly higher.
Prices were last at $5.11/$5.13, off two cents. But it was vulnerable to more losses if $5.10 support failed to hold again.
Palladium came under extra pressure following news that unions at Russia's Norilsk complex -- a major producer of the rare metal -- had promised to drop plans to disrupt output through June 30.
Palladium at one point were indicated as low as $141.50 an ounce, a decline of $6.25 from Monday's London close.
It then bounced slightly to around $143.00/$144.00.
Platinum, also produced at Norilsk, was also indicated easier at $372.00/$373.00, down $3.00.
